Class UnicodeUtils

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.util.UnicodeUtils
public final class UnicodeUtils extends Object
Utility constants and helpers for rendering mathematical and Greek text using Unicode code points instead of a custom font or markup.

The class exposes three things:

  • A large set of named String constants for individual Unicode characters (Greek letters, sub/superscripts, operators, arrows, ...).
  • specialCharReplace(String), which rewrites a small set of LaTeX-like escapes (e.g. \alpha, \leq) into the matching Unicode characters.
  • getSuperscript(int, boolean), which renders an integer using superscript digit glyphs.

All members are static; the class is not meant to be instantiated.

Implementation notes

The replacement set and the superscript digits are kept in small lookup tables (SPECIAL_CHAR_REPLACEMENTS and SUPERSCRIPT_DIGITS) rather than being hard-coded into the method bodies. The public constants and method signatures are unchanged, so this is a drop-in replacement.

  • Method Details

    • specialCharReplace

      public static String specialCharReplace(String s)
      Replace the LaTeX-like escape sequences in the given string with their Unicode equivalents.

      Recognized escapes include the Greek letters (\alpha, \Omega, ...) and a selection of math operators and arrows (\leq, \approx, \rarrow, ...). See SPECIAL_CHAR_REPLACEMENTS for the full set. Unrecognized text, including unknown backslash sequences, is left untouched.

      Replacement is purely textual and applied in table order, so an escape that forms the prefix of a longer one is handled before the shorter one.

      Parameters:
      s - the input string; may be null
      Returns:
      null if s is null; otherwise s with every recognized escape replaced by its Unicode character

    • getSuperscript

      public static String getSuperscript(int n, boolean isNegative)
      Render an integer's digits as Unicode superscript characters.

      The sign is supplied separately via isNegative rather than being read from n; callers normally pass the magnitude in n. Only the decimal digits 0-9 are converted, so any non-digit character in the textual form of n (such as a leading minus from a negative value) is ignored.

      Parameters:
      n - the number whose digits are rendered as superscripts
      isNegative - if true, a superscript minus sign is prepended
      Returns:
      the superscript representation, e.g. getSuperscript(12, true) returns "⁻¹²"
